newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's ruling Islamists deny president warning.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's ruling Islamists deny president warning.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan denied on Thursday that President Suleyman Demirel had sent him a letter expressing concern the Islamist-led government was increasingly at odds with the country's secular system.
Several local newspapers published on Thursday excerpts from the alleged letter, but Erbakan called the reports "a lie." The president's office declined comment.

"There is a widespread feeling that you are diverting from the secularist, democratic republican aims. This is also my belief," the mass-selling Hurriyet daily quoted President Suleyman Demirel as saying in the letter.
"If you continue with this attitude the regime will be in danger," the paper said Demirel wrote to Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader.

The newspapers said the alleged letter was also copied to armed forces leader Ismail Hakki Karadayi on the eve of a crucial meeting later this week between top politicians and the restive chiefs of the secularist armed forces.
"No, it is all a lie," Erbakan told reporters ahead of a cabinet meeting in Ankara.

An official from the president's office declined to comment on whether the letter had been sent. She said Demirel and Erbakan were to hold a regular meeting at the presidential palace on Thursday, scheduled for 5.00 p.m. (1500 GMT).

The armed forces have warned Erbakan's Islamist-right coalition in recent weeks against increasing the role of Islam in public life, and these issues are expected to be discussed at Friday's meeting of the National Security Council.
Opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz on Wednesday called for an alliance of all parties except Erbakan's Welfare Party to evade the danger of the military staging a fourth coup since 1960.
Demirel, himself dislodged as premier during two of the three previous coups, allegedly warned Erbakan against the consequences of upsetting the army and other groups.
He also told Erbakan in the letter quoted by Hurriyet that he would not approve any law that went against the principles of a secular, democratic republic.
